p2.tell: The axis starts at 19¢, and the bars compare April 2025, before the summer spike, with July 2026, 15 months later. July to July, prices rose 0.3%.
p2.explanation: Real EIA numbers, framed to mislead. A cropped axis makes a 26.5% gap look like a cliff, and cherry-picked months turn an old jump into a 'one year' rise. Prices did jump in 2025. Over the past year they've been nearly flat.
p2.con_line_fooled: Real numbers, honest-looking bars. I just picked where they start.
p2.con_line_caught: Fine. You checked the data. I'll crop it better next time.

p1.explanation: Real and word for word. 'No net increase' means some charges go up and others go down: Atlantic City Electric's bill rises $4.09 from some charges and falls $4.14 from others.
p1.con_line_false_alarm: That one was real. 'Net' is doing a lot of work, but it's true.

p3.explanation: Startling, but true: it's straight from the BPU's own press release. Bills jumped in 2025, and that's the rise the chart smuggled into its window.
p3.con_line_false_alarm: Surprising isn't the same as fake. A grain of salt, not the whole shaker.

p4.explanation: Real and word for word, from New Jersey Monitor's coverage of a BPU vote.
p4.con_line_false_alarm: Real. Not everything that sounds dramatic is a trick.
